incident.text: Employers generally have no warning when an employee may approach a manager or HR representative to file a complaint. In fact, most often the employee will simply be coming in to have a discussion, which turns into a complaint of wrongdoing that requires an investigation. For this reason, the information used to complete the incident report may be provided by the reporter at the time the incident report is completed, or may be reconstructed from notes taken at the initial meeting by the HR representative or manager who met with the employee. The important factor is that all of the information is complete and accurately reflects the initial complaint. Further details on the incident will be obtained through the interview process.
incident.title: About the Incident Report

plan.text: The Investigation Plan is an important tool used to prove that the company met the requirement of thinking through the investigation process, and created a detailed, comprehensive and unbiased plan before the investigation began. By following the plan, the investigator stays on track throughout the investigation, without changing course based on information received from one source or pre-conceived determination made before all parties are interviewed and assessed.
plan.title: About the Investigation Plan

notice.text: All parties to an investigation must be notified that there is a formal internal investigation taking place, of their role in the investigation and when and where they will be interviewed. The following employee notices provide that information, as well as the company’s expectations of cooperation and the legal rights of the employees. Please click on print/view notice to review the information and ensure that the auto-filled information is correct. You may then print the notice and deliver it to the employee to be signed, or select email notice and the notice will be sent to the interviewee with instructions to print the notice, sign it, and return it to the investigator within 48 hours of receipt.
notice.title: About the Notices to Interviewees

assessment.text:
Assessing the information and evidence provided in order to make a final determination can often be the most difficult part of an investigation. At this point it is more crucial than ever to set aside feelings and opinions and evaluate only the facts. All things must be considered such as:

1. The credibility of the witnesses,
2. The authenticity of any evidence provided.
3. The likelihood of the information provided being correct based on the witnesses’ proximity to the incident.
4. The consistency of the facts and details provided.

Often it is helpful to put yourself in the mindset of a criminal investigator. It is not the investigators job to determine the punishment, only to follow the evidence in making a determination if wrongdoing has occurred. And if so, as to the guilt of the accused party. The determinations must be made strictly on the assessment of the facts. In some cases, there is simply not enough evidence to make a determination one way or the other. It is acceptable to have the findings in the investigation be inconclusive but be careful not to use this as an easy out. Remember that the purpose of the investigation is to improve workplace conduct rather than to prepare for potential litigation. There can and likely will be other investigations, and you do not want to overlook or discard important facts in this investigation which may set a precedence for doing the same in the future. Now, go to a quiet place where you will not be interrupted and carefully read through the details provided below from the incident report through the interviews. Then respond to each statement by selecting yes, no or inconclusive. Include notes on what led you to that determination. These final responses and notes will all be included in the final determination summary that will be presented to the decision maker which allows for the appropriate actions to be determined.
assessment.title: About the Assessment

actions.text:
There are five items to be considered when determining the appropriate actions to take as a result of the workplace investigation. Prior to making these decisions, it is important to ensure that personal feelings toward the participants do not enter in to the decision making process. All corrective and preventive action decisions must be based strictly on the findings from the investigation. Consider the following, then choose the appropriate actions. Disciplinary action options are also included for the reporter, witnesses and victim, to be used only in the case of a false claim or when false information is provided during the interviews.

  • Severity – Was the conduct a single incident or a pattern? If a single incident, was it severe enough to warrant disciplinary acton?
  • Past Performance Does the respondent have a history of conduct or performance that is similar to what is being investigated?
  • Company Policy – Does the company have clearly written and communicated company policies that outline standards of conduct, prohibited behaviors and/or progressive discipline that may apply in this decision making process?
  • Evidence – Is there clear evidence or corroborative witness testimony sufficient enough to warrant disciplinary action?
  • Consistency – Has the company experienced similar incidents with similar investigative outcomes? If so, it is critical to take consistent actions to ensure non-discrimination. However, if this investigation finds the misconduct to be more severe or pervasive, or if company policy has been revised since the prior incidents, those items may be considered in the corrective action decisions and should be noted as such.
actions.title: About the Corrective and Preventive Actions

conclusion.text: Upon conclusion of a workplace investigation, the victim and the respondent are entitled to a written notice of the final findings. These notices are quite brief, and do not provide details of the investigation. As is often the case, you may be approached by the victim and/or the respondent asking for additional information on the investigation, such as details from the interviews or corrective actions taken. They may even request a complete copy of the investigation file. However, the details of the investigation, including the final report, are confidential company information and we do not suggest releasing copies without a subpoena and  consulting with an attorney. When approached by the participants in the investigation, it is best to express your understanding of why they would like to receive details, but that the company will respect the privacy of all parties involved and not discuss the situation further. This is also a good chance to remind the participants that if there are any further incidents or signs of retaliation, they should report the information to their manager or HR immediately.
conclusion.title: About the Conclusion Notices

hearing.text: Hearings of several different kinds can be required in an investigation. The most common types are Pre-Interview or Post-determination hearings required by collective bargaining agreements. But they may also include mediation hearings or public hearings as required. The Hearings module is used to record information, documents and notes that will be included in the Final Report as part of the investigation.
hearing.title: About Hearings

claim.text: Legal claims may come in the form of letters from government agencies such as the EEOC, State Employment Departments, or OSHA, or from independent attorneys. In most cases, these notices or action come after the conclusion of the investigation, so the Claims module remains open after the investigation has been closed. The Claims module can be used at any time to record information, documents and notes pertaining to any claim, and any form of settlement that takesplace. This information is kept as a seperate record and does not become a part of the investigaiton Final Report.
claim.title: About Claims

closeinvestigation.text: In some cases, it is not necessary to continue moving forward with an investigation. If that is the case, you may choose to stop an investigation at any step in the process. Once stopped, you will be prompted to document the reason for stopping the investigation.
closeinvestigation.title: About Closing the Investigation
